summary: Takanori Shintani is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977). He later held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1996–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010–2018).

Takao Hayashi is an Indology and history scholar. Educated at Tohoku, Kyoto, and Brown universities under David Pingree, Otto Neugebauer, Abraham Sachs, and Gerald J. Toomer, he held posts at Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and Doshisha University (1986–1989; 1995–2015).

Takao Kagawa was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University and taught Satoshi Hiraoka.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held faculty posts at Rissho University (attested 1972, 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984, 2001), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu was an Iranian, Central Asian, and history scholar educated at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University. He held faculty posts at Kanazawa University, Osaka University (1984; 1994–2012), Kindai University, Kobe City University of Foreign Studies, and Toyo Bunko.

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1951–1960). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1970–2002) and served as president of the Society for Indian Philosophy and Religion (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda and Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler, Lambert Schmithausen, Akira Hirakawa, and Ernst Steinkellner. He taught Florin Deleanu and held academic posts at Waseda University (~1988–2015; attested 2012–2026).
Takashi Maeda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University (~1969–1975). He held lecturer posts at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

Takashi Nakao is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who studied at Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Bunkyo University Women's College, the Society for the Study of Diplomatics in Japan, and Rissho University (1979–2002).

Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University (1986–1989), and the University of Tokyo. In 1991, he held an assistant professor post at Komazawa University.
Takashi Yamada is a sinology and religious studies scholar who studied at Hosei University. He held an assistant professor post at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a professorship at Komazawa University, attested in 1981 and 1991.
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979. He held a researcher post at Taisho University (attested 1978).

Takayasu Higuchi was an archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942). He was Professor of Archaeology at Kyoto University (~1968–1983) and directed Sen-oku Hakuko Kan, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Sen-oku Matsurokan, and Institute of Silk Road Studies.

Takayasu Kimura is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. In 1995, he held posts at the Institute for Contemporary Edification, Shingon-shu Buzan-ha, and Taisho University.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1985–1994). He served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (~2008).

Takayoshi Kamei was a history and Japanology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1912) and taught Hajime Nakamura. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1947), Ibaraki University (~1949–1961), and Seisen University (~1961–1974).

Takayoshi Namikawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed his degrees at Bukkyo University. He was a professor (1981) and professor emeritus (2018) at Bukkyo University, with additional posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University and Hokkaido University.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He held posts at Taisho University as a group member (until 1991) and professor (attested 2014).

Takehiro Sueki was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1942–1945). He held posts at the University of Electro-Communications (~1954–1965), the University of Tokyo (~1965–1982), and Toyo University (~1982–1992).
